title: LSM write path: two cheap appends, then acknowledge
caption: Nothing is updated in place. Flushing and compaction happen in the background, off the request path.

steps.text: 1. Append the mutation to the commit log: a sequential write to disk, so a crash can replay it.
2. Insert it into the memtable, an in-memory structure sorted by partition and clustering key.
3. Acknowledge. The replica has done one sequential append and one memory write: tens of microseconds.
4. Later, when the memtable reaches its size limit, it is written out as an immutable sorted file (SSTable) and the commit log segment is dropped.
5. Background compaction merges SSTables, keeps the newest cell per key and drops expired tombstones, so reads touch fewer files.
